extracted.intended_audience: interested parties in antidumping and countervailing duty proceedings (exporters, producers, importers, petitioners, foreign governments, and counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for submitting comments, case briefs, rebuttals, hearing requests, and related filings in U.S. Department of Commerce antidumping and countervailing duty investigations and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidy determination elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce preliminarily determines a subsidy exists where there is a financial contribution by an 'authority' that gives rise to a benefit to the recipient, and the subsidy is specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections 771(5)(B) and (D) regarding financial contribution; 771(5)(E) regarding benefit; and 771(5A) regarding specificity. For full methodology see Preliminary Decision Memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of facts available and adverse inferences (AFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If necessary information is missing from the record and respondents did not act to the best of their ability to respond, Commerce may rely on facts otherwise available and draw an adverse inference in selecting among those facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections 776(a) and (b) of the Act and the 'Use of Facts Available and Adverse Inferences' section of the Preliminary Decision Memorandum. Application of total AFA can result in there being no calculations to disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-others rate (preliminary determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a preliminary determination, the estimated all-others rate for companies not individually examined shall equal the weighted average of the estimated subsidy (or dumping) rates established for those companies individually examined, excluding any zero and de minimis rates and any rates determined entirely under section 776.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to sections 703(d) and 705(c)(5)(A) of the Act. If all individually examined rates are zero, de minimis, or based entirely on facts otherwise available, Commerce may use any reasonable method to establish the all-others rate pursuant to 705(c)(5)(A)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of liquidation and cash deposit instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce will direct CBP to suspend liquidation of entries of subject merchandise entered (or withdrawn from warehouse) for consumption on or after the date of publication of the notice, and instruct CBP to require a cash deposit equal to the rates indicated in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accordance with section 703(d)(2) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.205(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure timing of calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce normally discloses to interested parties the calculations performed in connection with a preliminary (or final) determination within five days of its public announcement or publication of the notice, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: when Commerce preliminarily applied total AFA such that there are no calculations to disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification protocol when parties uncooperative
rubrics_metrics.description: If mandatory respondents and the foreign government do not provide requested information and are uncooperative, Commerce may preliminarily determine verification will not be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-cooperation may lead to AFA and skipping verification steps; see related sections in Preliminary Decision Memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope case and rebuttal briefs — filing and content (scope-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties may submit scope case and rebuttal briefs on the preliminary decision regarding the scope; deadlines are provided in the preliminary scope decision memorandum. For scope briefs, parties must file identical documents simultaneously on the records of the ongoing LTFV and CVD investigations; no new factual information or business proprietary information may be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identical simultaneous filing requirement; consult the preliminary scope decision memorandum for deadlines and the prohibition on new facts/BPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case briefs and rebuttal briefs — deadlines and required components
rubrics_metrics.description: Case briefs on non-scope issues must be submitted to the Assistant Secretary no later than 20 days after publication of the preliminary determination; rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs, may be filed not later than five days after the date for filing case briefs. Submissions must include (1) a table of contents listing each issue, and (2) a table of authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 19 CFR 351.309(c)(2) and (d)(2). Failure to follow format or deadlines may affect consideration of the arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive summary requirement and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce requests that interested parties provide at the beginning of their briefs a public executive summary for each issue raised in their briefs, and will use these public executive summaries as the basis for comment summaries in the Issues and Decision Memorandum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit each issue executive summary to no more than 450 words (not including citations). Include footnotes for relevant citations. Note prior encouragement (in other proceedings) was a single executive summary limited to five pages total including footnotes; here Commerce requests per-issue public executive summaries with the 450-word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including new factual information or business proprietary information in scope briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope case and rebuttal briefs may not include new factual information or business proprietary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must rely on the existing record for scope arguments; inclusion of new facts/BPI may render submissions non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing request content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties wishing to request a hearing (limited to issues raised in the case and rebuttal briefs) must submit a written request to the Assistant Secretary within 30 days after publication of the notice. The request must contain: (1) the party’s name, address, and telephone number; (2) the number of participants and whether any participant is a foreign national; and (3) a list of the issues to be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hearing is requested, Commerce intends to hold it at a time and date to be determined. Parties should confirm by telephone the date, time, and location two days before the scheduled date. See 19 CFR 351.310(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final determination timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to issue the final determination within 75 days after the date of its preliminary determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to section 705(a)(1) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.210(b)(1). Tolling (extensions) may apply under certain circumstances as noted elsewhere in notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and assessment procedures for administrative reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to disclose calculations performed in connection with final results to interested parties within five days after public announcement (or publication), and will assess antidumping duties on appropriate entries in accordance with the final results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 19 CFR 351.224(b) and section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act. Commerce may calculate importer-specific assessment rates based on the ratio of total dumping for examined sales to total entered value per 19 CFR 351.212(b)(1) and established precedents (e.g., 77 FR 8101 (Feb. 14, 2012) final modification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer-specific assessment and zero/de minimis treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the weighted-average dumping margins are not zero or de minimis, Commerce calculates an importer-specific assessment rate. If an importer-specific assessment rate is zero or de minimis (less than 0.50 percent), entries by that importer will be liquidated without regard to antidumping duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment rate calculation method described in 'Antidumping Proceedings: Calculation of the Weighted-Average Dumping Margin and Assessment Rate in Certain Antidumping Duty Proceedings; Final Modification' (77 FR 8101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of unreviewed entries sold through intermediaries
rubrics_metrics.description: For POR entries produced by individually examined respondents for which they did not know the merchandise sold to the intermediary was destined for the United States, Commerce will instruct CBP to liquidate unreviewed entries at the all-others rate if there is no rate for the intermediate company(ies) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the use of an all-others rate when intermediate parties were not reviewed and no company-specific rate exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of issuance of assessment instructions and stays if litigation filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication of the final results; if a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired (i.e., within 90 days of publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process preserves judicial remedies before liquidation where litigation is timely initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit rate rules after final results
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication of the notice, cash deposit requirements take effect: (1) company-specific cash deposit = company-specific weighted-average dumping margins from final results; (2) if exporter not covered in this review but covered in prior completed segment, continue that company-specific rate; (3) if exporter not covered but producer covered previously, deposit rate = most recent producer rate; (4) cash deposit for all other producers/exporters = all-others rate established in the investigation (adjusted where applicable). These cash deposit requirements remain in effect until further notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act and related notices. The all-others rate cited (example) is 1.95 percent adjusted for export-subsidy rate in companion CVD investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer notification re: reimbursement certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice serves as a reminder to importers of their responsibility under 19 CFR 351.402(f)(2) to file a certificate regarding reimbursement of antidumping and/or countervailing duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during the POR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply could result in Commerce’s presumption that reimbursement occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Protective Order (APO) obligations and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties subject to an APO must return or destroy proprietary information disclosed under APO in accordance with 19 CFR 351.305(a)(3); timely written notification of return/destruction or conversion to a judicial protective order is requested. Failure to comply with APO regulations and terms is a violation subject to sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice serves as a final reminder of APO responsibilities in this segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional measures and their duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of liquidation pursuant to an affirmative preliminary determination may not remain in effect more than four months, except exporters representing a significant proportion of exports may request extension to no more than six months. Collection of cash deposits at listed rates begins on the date of publication of the ITC’s final injury determinations; entries during the lapse of provisional measures (the period after provisional measures expire and before ITC final determination publication) will be liquidated without regard to antidumping duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 733(d) governs the four/six-month rule; Commerce's practice results in temporary termination of suspension for the lapse period and resumption upon ITC final determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of investigation — written description dispositive
rubrics_metrics.description: The written description of the merchandise in the scope is dispositive; HTSUS statistical reporting numbers are provided for convenience and customs purposes only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope describes product characteristics (e.g., sol gel alumina-based ceramic abrasive grains composition, grain sizes, shapes, crystalline properties) and clarifies coverage when incorporated into downstream articles (only the grain component is covered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Inquiry Service List (AISL) procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce will create an annual inquiry service list segment in ACCESS within five business days of publication of an order; interested parties who wish to be added must submit an entry of appearance in the AISL segment in ACCESS within 30 days after publication. A law firm with multiple attorneys should designate a lead attorney for ease of administration. Commerce will finalize the list within five business days thereafter and may update it as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AISL segment is named 'AISL-[Anniversary Month]' in ACCESS. Petitioners and foreign governments, once initially placed, are automatically included in subsequent years but remain responsible for amending entries during annual updates. Procedural Guidance and Final Rule references: 86 FR 52300 and 86 FR 53205.
